summary: Registers and documents the MIME types for JPEG 2000 images, the ISO/IEC 15444 family of formats. This lets applications label and recognize those files in mail, web and other contexts.

eli5.summary: Every kind of file needs a name tag so computers know what it is. This hands out the name tags for a particular type of picture.

subtitle: The official file type labels for JPEG 2000 images and videos.

tldr.problem: JPEG 2000 is a newer image compression standard designed to replace JPEG, but web browsers and email clients did not recognize its file types until they were officially registered.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers four MIME types with IANA: image/jp2 for basic JPEG 2000 still images, image/jpx for extended images, video/mj2 for motion sequences, and image/jpm for compound documents containing multiple types of media.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now correctly identify and handle JPEG 2000 files in all Internet contexts without guessing their format.

today: RFC 3745 is an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted. JPEG 2000 adoption has been strongest in specialized domains such as medical imaging and digital cinema, though JPEG remains dominant for consumer photography.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This RFC registers the official MIME types for JPEG 2000, which is defined by the ISO/IEC 15444 family of standards. The four MIME types are image/jp2, image/jpx, video/mj2, and image/jpm.

Unlike the older JPEG standard which was partially defined in multiple places, JPEG 2000 includes a complete file format specification as a required part of the standard. This RFC uses that specification to formally document how each image variant should be labeled on the Internet.
sections.eli5: JPEG 2000 is a newer way to store pictures using wavelet technology instead of the older JPEG method. When your computer downloads one, it needs a name tag so it knows what to do with it.

sections.title: JPEG 2000 Overview
sections.content:
JPEG 2000 is a modern image compression standard designed to improve upon the original JPEG in several ways. It uses wavelet-based compression, which provides better compression at very low bit rates and more graceful quality degradation. The standard defines both lossless compression (which preserves every pixel perfectly) and lossy compression (which discards some data to save space).

The standard supports many image types: bi-level (black and white), grayscale, color, and multi-component images from diverse sources including digital cameras, medical imaging systems, and satellite photography. It can handle images larger than 64,000 by 64,000 pixels without needing to split them into tiles.

JPEG 2000 is intentionally designed to complement rather than replace the original JPEG standard, which continues to dominate most applications.
sections.eli5: JPEG 2000 is a better way to shrink pictures without losing quality. It works for all kinds of pictures and can handle really huge ones.

sections.title: The MIME Type Registrations
sections.content:
Four MIME types are registered by this RFC, each corresponding to a different part of the JPEG 2000 standard.

image/jp2 refers to files that follow ISO/IEC 15444-1, the core JPEG 2000 specification. The file format is defined in Annex I of that standard. The recommended file extension is .jp2, though .jpg2 is also accepted. The magic number (the first bytes identifying the file type) is the 12-byte sequence: 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x0C 0x6A 0x50 0x20 0x20 0x0D 0x0A 0x87 0x0A.

image/jpx extends JPEG 2000 with additional features defined in ISO/IEC 15444-2. This type allows more sophisticated image processing features and optional metadata. The preferred file extension is .jpf (JPEG File format), though .jpx is also accepted.

video/mj2 is Motion JPEG 2000, defined in ISO/IEC 15444-3. This format uses the ISO Base Media File Format (also used by MP4) as its container and can store video sequences where each frame is a JPEG 2000 image. It can also carry audio. The file extensions are .mj2 (preferred) or .mjp2.

image/jpm is for Compound Image File Format (ISO/IEC 15444-6), which combines JPEG 2000 with support for rendering other types of content. This format uses the Multi-layer Mixed Raster Content imaging model to store compound documents such as scanned documents that might contain both photographs and text. The file extensions are .jpm (preferred) or .jpgm.
sections.eli5: There are four different name tags. One for plain pictures, one for fancier pictures with extra features, one for videos, and one for mixed documents that have pictures and other stuff together.

sections.title: Why JPEG 2000 Exists
sections.content:
The original JPEG standard (ISO/IEC 10918), defined in the 1990s, became ubiquitous but had limitations. It works well at medium to high compression ratios but performs poorly at very low bit rates and does not handle all image types equally well.

JPEG 2000 was designed to address these shortcomings using wavelet-based compression technology. It provides dramatically better compression at rates below 0.25 bits per pixel for grayscale images. It also has a unified architecture: while the original JPEG standard has 44 different coding modes (many unused), JPEG 2000 achieves flexibility through a single, cleaner decompression architecture that implementations can extend with additional parts.

JPEG 2000 includes a complete specification for file format as a mandatory part of the standard, unlike the original JPEG which split its definition across multiple documents and required the JFIF format specification for practical interchange.
sections.eli5: The old JPEG was invented in the 1990s and it was pretty good. But JPEG 2000 is better at making very tiny file sizes without looking bad, and it works the same way for all kinds of pictures.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
JPEG 2000 files can store image data and metadata such as information to help with viewing, rendering, and cataloging. These metadata fields are descriptive in nature and do not instruct recipient applications to perform any particular action, so they do not create additional security risks by themselves.

Some metadata fields may be intended to protect images against unauthorized use or distribution, such as copyright notices or digital rights information. Alteration or removal of such protective metadata may constitute an offense under World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) treaty agreements.

JPEG 2000 has an extensible structure, so it is theoretically possible that future metadata fields could induce particular actions in recipient applications. Currently, the specifications do not support such capabilities. For enhanced security, encryption, signing, or authentication can be applied using mechanisms defined in ISO/IEC 15444-8 (JPSEC, the security aspects part of JPEG 2000).
sections.eli5: The pictures themselves are safe. But someone could try to trick you by changing information that says who owns a picture. That's like forging a signature on a piece of paper.

sections.title: Status and Adoption
sections.content:
RFC 3745 is an Internet Standard. The MIME types it registers have become the official way to label JPEG 2000 files in email, on the web, and in other Internet applications.

JPEG 2000 adoption has been strongest in specialized domains: medical imaging, satellite imagery, digital cinema, and large-scale archival systems where the compression efficiency or lossless quality matter. It has not displaced JPEG for everyday consumer photography and web use, where JPEG remains dominant due to its simpler implementation and near-universal support.

All four MIME types (image/jp2, image/jpx, video/mj2, image/jpm) are now registered with IANA and available for use in standards, applications, and Internet protocols.
sections.eli5: The name tags are now official. JPEG 2000 is used by doctors and space agencies for very important pictures, but regular people still use the old JPEG for photos because it's simpler.
